chunks.title: Grease Fire Response
chunks.content: If a range top grease fire occurs, smother flames with a close-fitting lid or metal tray and turn off the burner, never use water, and evacuate and call the fire department if flames don't go out immediately.

steps: Smother flames with a close-fitting lid, cookie sheet, or metal tray
Do NOT use water, wet dishcloths, or towels
If flames do not go out immediately, evacuate and call the fire department
Only use a Class ABC extinguisher if fire is small, contained, and you can fight it with your back to an exit

chunks.title: Power Disconnect Before Service
chunks.content: Before servicing or cleaning the hood, switch off power at the service panel and lock or tag the disconnect to prevent accidental power-on, which could cause severe injury.

scenarios.condition: Before servicing or cleaning the unit
steps: Switch off power at the service panel
Lock the service disconnect to prevent accidental power-on
If it cannot be locked, attach a prominent warning tag to the panel

chunks.title: Ducting and Fire Hazard Warnings
chunks.content: Use only rigid metal ductwork vented to the outdoors; never terminate ducts inside walls, ceilings, attics, crawl spaces, or garages, as this creates a fire hazard.

chunks.title: Electrical Installation Requirements
chunks.content: Installation and wiring must be done by qualified persons per applicable codes; the hood requires a 120V 60Hz individual grounded branch circuit protected by a 15 or 20 amp breaker or time-delay fuse.

chunks.title: Tub/Shower and GFCI Requirement
chunks.content: If the unit is installed over a tub or shower, it must be marked appropriate for that application and connected to a GFCI-protected branch circuit.

chunks.title: Combustion Air and Backdrafting
chunks.content: Sufficient air is needed for proper combustion and exhausting of gases through the flue of fuel-burning equipment to prevent back drafting; follow NFPA/ASHRAE and local code guidelines.

chunks.title: Prop 65 and General Cautions
chunks.content: This product may contain chemicals known to California to cause cancer or reproductive harm; also, do not use the fan with any solid-state control device, and use it only for general ventilating (not hazardous/explosive materials).

chunks.title: Always Leave Filters and Grilles in Place
chunks.content: Always leave safety grilles and filters installed; without them, the operating blower could catch hair, fingers, or loose clothing.

chunks.title: Hood Dimensions and Mounting Heights
chunks.content: Standard duct cover: min ducted 30in, min recirculating 32in, max 42-1/2in; extension duct cover: min ducted 46-1/2in, min recirculating 50-1/2in, max 80in; ceiling heights range 90in to 150in depending on configuration.

chunks.title: Parts List and Materials
chunks.content: Included: hood, 2 aluminum mesh filters, duct cover assembly, duct cover wall bracket, 2 LumiLight LEDs (6W), single blower motor, hardware package with screws and wire nuts; not supplied: ducting, cable locking connector, duct cover extension, recirculating kit.

chunks.title: Ducting Calculation and Length Limits
chunks.content: Total duct length (accounting for elbows, transitions, caps as equivalent feet) should not exceed 150 equivalent feet; a ducting calculation sheet is provided to compute total run.

chunks.title: Ducting Best Practices
chunks.content: Use rigid 6" round metal duct minimum (7" for long runs), avoid flexible duct (restricts airflow up to 50%), minimize elbows/transitions, and keep mounting height between 24" min and 34" max above range top.

chunks.title: Mount the Hood
chunks.content: Measure and mark centerlines and mounting height (12-1/4in above range line, 26in min from range top), fasten mounting screws into studs (add blocking or approved anchors if no studs), hang the hood, secure with additional screws, then attach the duct cover bracket to the wall.

chunks.title: Complete Installation: Ducting, Power, Duct Covers
chunks.content: After mounting, secure the air diverter plate if using recirculating mode, install ductwork and seal all joints with certified duct tape, power up the hood and check for leaks, then extend and secure the telescopic duct covers to the wall bracket with M4x8 screws.

chunks.title: Install Ductless Recirculation Kit
chunks.content: Purchase the ZRC-01OM recirculating kit, secure the air diverter plate to the wall below the duct cover bracket, attach charcoal filters to the back of the aluminum mesh filters using the supplied brackets, reinstall the mesh filters, then enable recirculating mode on the control panel.

chunks.title: Touch Control Basics
chunks.content: The power button turns the whole hood on/off and remembers last fan/light settings; fan speed buttons cycle Q(uiet), 2, 3, 4; lights toggle between high, low, and off.

chunks.title: Delay Off Timer
chunks.content: With the fan on, press and hold the power button for two seconds to drop the fan to speed 1 and start a 5-minute delay-off timer; pressing power again cancels it immediately.

chunks.title: Enable Recirculating Mode on Controls
chunks.content: With the hood off, press and hold the '+' and light buttons simultaneously for three seconds to enable recirculating mode (clean filter indicator illuminates 3 seconds); repeat to disable (indicator blinks twice).

chunks.title: Verify or Set Maximum Fan CFM (ACT™)
chunks.content: With hood off, hold the power button for 3-5 seconds to display max CFM (speed 4=default, speed 3=390 CFM, speed 2=290 CFM); installers change this by repositioning a plastic jumper on the PC board before installation, and the setting cannot be changed again after power-up.

chunks.title: Clean Stainless and Black Stainless Steel Surfaces
chunks.content: Clean periodically with warm soapy water and a cotton or microfiber cloth, rubbing in the direction of the grain; use a liquid degreaser for heavy grease and a non-abrasive stainless polish afterward (but never on black stainless, which has an anti-smudge coating).

chunks.title: Clean Aluminum Mesh Filters
chunks.content: Remove the aluminum mesh filters and clean by hand or in the dishwasher with a non-phosphate detergent; spray with degreaser and let soak if heavily soiled, then dry and reinstall before use.

chunks.title: Replace Charcoal Filters (Recirculating Mode)
chunks.content: In recirculating mode, the clean filter indicator flashes after 120 hours of use indicating the charcoal filters need replacement (part Z0F-C091, 2 per hood); charcoal filters cannot be washed.

chunks.title: Replace LumiLight LED
chunks.content: Remove the mesh filter, remove side panels and light panel screws, disconnect the LED quick connector, push in the two side clips, and push the LED through the light panel opening for replacement.

chunks.title: Unit Doesn't Work / Blower or Light Issues
chunks.content: Covers unit not powering on, light working but blower not turning, unit vibrating, and unit whistling, with causes ranging from power/wiring issues to a defective blower or thermal protection trip.

rows: Power not on / wiring disconnected / defective board
Check breaker/power, verify connections, replace defective board
Blower wire disconnected, thermal protection tripped, defective board, seized blower
Check wiring, allow cooldown, replace defective part
Blower not secured, damaged wheel, hood not secured
Filter misaligned or duct connections not sealed
Adjust filter position, check duct seals

chunks.title: LumiLight LED Not Working
chunks.content: If the blower works but the LEDs don't, check for a disconnected LumiLight connector, a defective LED, or a defective switch/control board.

rows: Change the switch board or control board

chunks.title: Hood Not Venting Properly / Filter Vibrating
chunks.content: Poor venting can result from wrong duct size, hood mounted too high, outside wind interference, or blockage in ductwork; a vibrating mesh filter may be loose or have a broken spring clip.

rows: Filter loose or spring clip broken

chunks.title: Wiring Diagram Overview
chunks.content: Shows connections between motor, control board, condenser (12.5+12.5µF 250V), LEDs, and 120V 60Hz AC power supply with body/ground, black, and white wire designations.

chunks.title: Parts and Accessories List
chunks.content: Replacement parts include LumiLight LED (Z0B0047) and aluminum mesh filter (50200059); optional accessories include Make-up Air Kit (MUA006A), duct cover extensions in stainless (Z1C-01OMS) or black stainless (Z1C-01OMBS), recirculating kit (ZRC-01OM), replacement charcoal filter (Z0F-C091), and baffle filter kit (Z0F-B002).

tasks.title: Clean Aluminum Mesh Filters
tasks.description: Wash the removable aluminum mesh grease filters by hand or in the dishwasher to keep grease from accumulating.
tasks.justification: Grease buildup on filters is a fire hazard and reduces airflow/performance.
tasks.instructions_text: Remove the aluminum mesh filters from the hood. Wash by hand or in the dishwasher using a non-phosphate detergent, spraying with degreaser and soaking first if heavily soiled. Dry thoroughly and reinstall before using the hood again.

tasks.title: Reset Mesh Filter Clean Indicator
tasks.description: Reset the 30-hour clean filter timer on the control panel after washing the mesh filters.
tasks.justification: Keeps the indicator accurate so the reminder continues to reflect real usage.
tasks.instructions_text: With the hood off, hold the fan speed decrease button ('-') for three seconds. The clean filters indicator will turn off, confirming the 30-hour timer has been reset.

tasks.title: Replace Charcoal Filters
tasks.description: Replace the charcoal odor-filtering filters when using the hood in ductless recirculating mode.
tasks.justification: Spent charcoal filters no longer purify exhaust fumes, allowing odors and smoke to recirculate into the home.
tasks.instructions_text: When the clean filters indicator flashes on and off (after about 120 hours of use in recirculating mode), remove the old charcoal filters from the back of the mesh filters and attach new ones (part Z0F-C091) using the supplied brackets. Reset the 120-hour timer by holding the '+' button for three seconds with the hood off.

tasks.title: Clean Stainless Steel Surfaces
tasks.description: Wipe down the hood's stainless or black stainless exterior to remove grease and keep the finish looking good.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic only — prevents grease buildup and fingerprints from dulling the finish.
tasks.instructions_text: Wipe with warm soapy water and a cotton or microfiber cloth in the direction of the grain. Use a liquid degreaser for heavier grease buildup, then a non-abrasive stainless polish to buff (skip the polish step on black stainless, which has an anti-smudge coating).

tasks.title: Level and Mount the Hood
tasks.description: Mark centerlines, mounting heights, and secure the hood to wall studs (or approved anchors) at installation.
tasks.justification: Improper mounting can cause the hood to fall, damage the cooktop/counter, or create a fire/heat hazard if mounted too low.
tasks.instructions_text: Measure up from the range top (minimum 26in) and mark the mounting height and centerline. Drive mounting screws into wall studs (adding wood blocking or approved wall anchors if no studs are present), hang the hood, and secure it with additional screws from inside. Center and attach the duct cover wall bracket below the ceiling or soffit.

re_check_triggers.description: Hood feels loose, shifts, or vibrates during use

tasks.title: Install and Seal Ductwork
tasks.description: Install rigid metal ductwork from the hood to the outside and seal all joints, then check for leaks.
tasks.justification: Unsealed or improperly sized ductwork reduces exhaust performance and can allow moisture/grease to accumulate in walls or ceilings, creating a fire hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: Use rigid single-wall metal ductwork only (6" round minimum), fasten connections with sheet metal screws, and tape all joints with certified silver or duct tape. Power up the hood afterward and check around the tape for air leaks.

re_check_triggers.description: Smoke or odors are not being effectively pulled outside

tasks.title: Verify Electrical Grounding and Circuit
tasks.description: Confirm the hood is connected to a properly grounded, dedicated 120V branch circuit with correct breaker/fuse protection.
tasks.justification: Improper grounding or an undersized circuit creates a shock or fire hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: A qualified electrician should verify the hood is wired to an individual, properly grounded branch circuit protected by a 15 or 20 amp breaker or time-delay fuse, using 2-wire-with-ground wiring, and install a cable locking connector if required by local code.

re_check_triggers.description: Burning smell, sparks, tripped breaker, or shock when touching the unit

tasks.title: Set Maximum Blower CFM (ACT™)
tasks.description: Configure the airflow control jumper on the PC board to limit maximum blower CFM to comply with local codes, if required.
tasks.justification: Some local codes restrict maximum exhaust CFM without makeup air; skipping this on a code-restricted install can violate code requirements.
tasks.instructions_text: Before installing the hood, remove the mesh filters and PC board cover, reposition the plastic jumper to the desired CFM setting (390 or 290), and reinstall the board. Apply the corresponding foil CFM sticker inside the hood body near the wiring diagram as a permanent record.

tasks.title: Install Recirculating Kit Components
tasks.description: Secure the air diverter plate and attach charcoal filters when configuring the hood for ductless recirculating operation instead of venting outside.
tasks.justification: Missing diverter plate or charcoal filters prevents proper air purification and recirculation, reducing odor and smoke removal.
tasks.instructions_text: Purchase the recirculating kit (ZRC-01OM), secure the air diverter plate to the wall below the duct cover bracket, attach charcoal filters to the back of the aluminum mesh filters with the supplied brackets, and reinstall the mesh filters. Then enable recirculating mode on the touch controls.

weekly.title: Weekly Exterior Cleaning
steps: Wipe stainless or black stainless surfaces with warm soapy water and a cotton or microfiber cloth, rubbing in the direction of the grain
Use a liquid degreaser detergent for heavier grease build-up
On regular stainless, buff with a non-abrasive stainless polish (skip on black stainless)
supplies: Non-abrasive stainless steel polish (not for black stainless)

deep_clean.title: Filter Deep Clean
steps: Remove the aluminum mesh filters from the hood
Wash by hand or in the dishwasher with a non-phosphate detergent
Spray with degreasing detergent and let soak if heavily soiled
Reinstall filters before using the hood
If in recirculating mode, also inspect/replace charcoal filters (do not wash charcoal filters)
